title: The city streets beneath our feet
titleChinese: 我们脚下深处的城市街道
paragraphs: Stand outside Chancery Lane Tube station in London and you'll probably notice the regular commuters, trendy cafes and the odd tourist. Look up and you'll see the Staple Inn, built in 1585, and one of the last remaining Tudor timber-framed facades in London. But deep below your feet, there's more history lurking.

Nestled between Furnival Street and Fulwood Place in this area of London are a network of tunnels even deeper than The London Underground. Built between 1940 and 1942, the tunnels were constructed as part of the war effort as an air-raid shelter, designed to protect civilians and soldiers from bombs dropped in the war. Later in World War Two, the tunnels were occupied by Special Operations Executive and are even believed to have been the inspiration behind Q branch in the James Bond novels. The tunnels are set to open to the public in the near future.

Somewhere that can never open to the public is a secret Victorian street in Bristol. Now considered too dangerous to enter, a local historian climbed down to the street in 1999. He hoped to find gas street lamps, sash window frames and Victorian fire grates frozen in time. Instead, he found thieves had stripped the street, and it was mostly full of rubbish, though some bricked-up shop windows remained. The row of shops was buried in 1879 when a railway was built, and the company raised the road level.

In Scotland, there is an even older piece of history under foot. Mary King's Close in the centre of Edinburgh is a hidden network of preserved streets and homes from the 1600s. Down under the Royal Mile, the alleyways were once bustling and open-air but also dark and rather smelly. Many Old Town Edinburgh streets in the 1600s consisted of high-tenement buildings where the rich occupied the top stories and the poor lived on the ground floors, which were often flooded with sewage. The streets on Mary King's Close were built over in the 1750s and only rediscovered in 2003 during an archaeological investigation. It's now a tourist attraction, so you can go down and see the streets for yourself.
So, when you're out and about in the city, admire what's above ground, but also consider the history that could be hiding beneath your feet.
chineseParagraphs: 站在伦敦钱塞里巷地铁站外，你很可能会注意到日常通勤者、时尚咖啡馆和偶尔出现的游客。抬头望去，你会看到建于1585年的斯台普尔旅馆，它是伦敦仅存的几座都铎时代木框架结构建筑之一。但在你脚下深处，还潜藏着更多历史。
位于伦敦这一区域的弗尼瓦尔街和弗尔伍德广场之间，隐藏着一个比伦敦地铁还要深的隧道网络。这些隧道建于1940年至1942年间，是二战期间作为防空洞而建造的，旨在保护平民和士兵免受战争空袭炸弹的伤害。二战后期，这些隧道由特别行动处接管，甚至被认为是詹姆斯·邦德小说中Q部门的灵感来源。这些隧道计划于不久的将来向公众开放。
在布里斯托尔，有一条永远无法向公众开放的隐秘维多利亚时代街道。由于现在被认为过于危险而无法进入，一位当地历史学家曾在1999年下到这条街道。他希望找到那些经久未变的煤气街灯、上下推拉窗框和维多利亚时代的壁炉栅。然而，他发现街道已被盗贼洗劫一空，大部分地方堆满了垃圾，尽管仍有一些用砖堵上的商店橱窗。这排商店在1879年因修建铁路而被掩埋，铁路公司当时抬高了路面。

在苏格兰，脚下还有更古老的历史遗迹。爱丁堡市中心的玛丽·金小巷是17世纪保存完好的街道和住宅构成的隐秘网络。在皇家大道地下，这些小巷曾经熙熙攘攘，是露天的，但也阴暗且气味难闻。17世纪爱丁堡老城的许多街道由高高的公寓楼组成，富人住在顶层，而穷人则住在常常被污水淹没的一楼。玛丽·金小巷的街道在18世纪50年代被新建筑覆盖，直到2003年的一次考古调查中才被重新发现。如今，它已成为一个旅游景点，你可以亲自下去一睹这些街道的风采。
所以，当你在城市里外出走动时，不妨欣赏地面上的风景，但也请想一想可能隐藏在你脚下的历史。

vocabulary.definition: 通勤者，上下班往返的人
vocabulary.entry: commuter /kəˈmjuːtə(r)/ n. 通勤者，上下班往返的人
vocabulary.example: The train was packed with commuters.
vocabulary.translation: 火车上挤满了通勤者。

vocabulary.entry: trendy /ˈtrendi/ adj. 时髦的，流行的（口语）
vocabulary.example: This area has become very trendy among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区在年轻人中变得非常时髦。

vocabulary.entry: odd /ɒd/ adj. 偶尔的，零星的
vocabulary.example: He makes the odd mistake when he's tired.
vocabulary.translation: 他累了的时候会偶尔犯点错。

vocabulary.definition: 都铎王朝的（历史专有名词）
vocabulary.entry: Tudor /ˈtjuːdə(r)/ adj. 都铎王朝的（历史专有名词）
vocabulary.example: The house is a fine example of Tudor architecture.
vocabulary.translation: 这所房子是都铎建筑的优秀范例。

vocabulary.entry: timber-framed /ˈtɪmbə freɪmd/ adj. 木框架结构的
vocabulary.example: The village is full of timber-framed cottages.
vocabulary.translation: 这个村庄到处都是木框架结构的小屋。

vocabulary.entry: facade /fəˈsɑːd/ n. （建筑物的）正面，立面（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The building's facade was beautifully decorated.
vocabulary.translation: 建筑物的正面装饰得很漂亮。

vocabulary.entry: lurk /lɜːk/ v. 潜伏，潜藏（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Danger lurks beneath the surface.
vocabulary.translation: 危险潜藏于表面之下。

vocabulary.definition: 坐落于，位于（安静或隐蔽处）（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: nestled /ˈnesld/ adj. 坐落于，位于（安静或隐蔽处）（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The village is nestled in a valley.
vocabulary.translation: 这个村庄坐落在一个山谷里。

vocabulary.entry: air-raid shelter /ˈeə reɪd ˌʃeltə(r)/ n. 防空洞（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: During the war, people took cover in air-raid shelters.
vocabulary.translation: 战争期间，人们躲进防空洞。

vocabulary.entry: civilian /səˈvɪliən/ n. 平民，百姓（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The army was ordered to protect civilians.
vocabulary.translation: 军队奉命保护平民。

vocabulary.definition: 被占据的，被占领的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: occupied /ˈɒkjupaɪd/ adj. 被占据的，被占领的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The building was occupied by the army.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑被军队占领了。

vocabulary.definition: 特别行动处（二战英国情报机构，专有名词）
vocabulary.entry: Special Operations Executive /ˌspeʃl ˌɒpəˈreɪʃnz ɪɡˈzekjətɪv/ n. 特别行动处（二战英国情报机构，专有名词）
vocabulary.example: The Special Operations Executive carried out secret missions during the war.
vocabulary.translation: 特别行动处在战争期间执行了秘密任务。

vocabulary.definition: 灵感，启发灵感的人或事
vocabulary.entry: inspiration /ˌɪnspəˈreɪʃn/ n. 灵感，启发灵感的人或事
vocabulary.example: The beautiful scenery provided the inspiration for his painting.
vocabulary.translation: 美丽的景色为他的画作提供了灵感。

vocabulary.entry: set to /ˌset ˈtu/ phr. v. 即将，准备（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The company is set to launch its new product next month.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司将于下月推出新产品。

vocabulary.definition: 维多利亚时代的（历史专有名词）
vocabulary.entry: Victorian /vɪkˈtɔːriən/ adj. 维多利亚时代的（历史专有名词）
vocabulary.example: The city has many Victorian buildings.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市有许多维多利亚时代的建筑。

vocabulary.entry: sash window /ˈsæʃ ˌwɪndəʊ/ n. 上下推拉窗（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The old house still has its original sash windows.
vocabulary.translation: 这栋老房子还保留着原来的上下推拉窗。

vocabulary.entry: frame /freɪm/ n. 框架，边框
vocabulary.example: The picture has a beautiful wooden frame.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画有一个漂亮的木框。

vocabulary.entry: fire grate /ˈfaɪə ɡreɪt/ n. 壁炉炉栅（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The fire grate was filled with burning coals.
vocabulary.translation: 壁炉炉栅里装满了燃烧的煤。

vocabulary.definition: 经久不变的，定格在时间中（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: frozen in time /ˌfrəʊzn ɪn ˈtaɪm/ phr. 经久不变的，定格在时间中（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The abandoned village was frozen in time.
vocabulary.translation: 这个被遗弃的村庄定格在时间中。

vocabulary.entry: strip /strɪp/ v. 洗劫，剥去（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The thieves stripped the house of all valuables.
vocabulary.translation: 盗贼洗劫了房子里所有值钱的东西。

vocabulary.entry: bricked-up /ˈbrɪkt ʌp/ adj. 用砖堵住的
vocabulary.example: The windows were bricked-up to prevent entry.
vocabulary.translation: 窗户用砖堵住了以防止进入。

vocabulary.entry: row /rəʊ/ n. 一排（建筑物）
vocabulary.example: There is a row of shops on the high street.
vocabulary.translation: 商业街上有一排商店。

vocabulary.entry: raise /reɪz/ v. 抬高，提升
vocabulary.example: The floor was raised to prevent flooding.
vocabulary.translation: 地板被抬高了以防洪水。

vocabulary.entry: close /kləʊz/ n. （苏格兰）小巷，死胡同
vocabulary.example: Mary King's Close is a famous historic site in Edinburgh.
vocabulary.translation: 玛丽·金小巷是爱丁堡著名的历史遗址。

vocabulary.entry: preserved /prɪˈzɜːvd/ adj. 保存完好的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The house is perfectly preserved.
vocabulary.translation: 这所房子保存得完好无损。

vocabulary.entry: alleyway /ˈæliweɪ/ n. 小巷，胡同
vocabulary.example: The alleyway was narrow and dark.
vocabulary.translation: 这条小巷又窄又暗。

vocabulary.definition: 熙熙攘攘的，热闹的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: bustling /ˈbʌslɪŋ/ adj. 熙熙攘攘的，热闹的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The market was bustling with shoppers.
vocabulary.translation: 市场上购物者熙熙攘攘。

vocabulary.entry: open-air /ˌəʊpən ˈeə(r)/ adj. 露天的，户外的
vocabulary.example: The concert was held in an open-air theatre.
vocabulary.translation: 音乐会在露天剧场举行。

vocabulary.definition: 公寓楼，出租屋（尤指苏格兰或美国）（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: tenement /ˈtenəmənt/ n. 公寓楼，出租屋（尤指苏格兰或美国）（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Many old tenement buildings have been renovated.
vocabulary.translation: 许多旧公寓楼已被翻新。

vocabulary.entry: occupy /ˈɒkjupaɪ/ v. 占据，占用（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The sofa occupies too much space in the room.
vocabulary.translation: 沙发在房间里占太多空间。

vocabulary.entry: storey /ˈstɔːri/ n. 楼层（英式）
vocabulary.example: They live in a flat on the third storey.
vocabulary.translation: 他们住在四楼的公寓里。

vocabulary.entry: sewage /ˈsuːɪdʒ/ n. 污水，污物（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The sewage system needs to be repaired.
vocabulary.translation: 污水系统需要维修。

vocabulary.definition: 考古的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: archaeological /ˌɑːkiəˈlɒdʒɪkl/ adj. 考古的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Archaeological remains were found at the site.
vocabulary.translation: 在该遗址发现了考古遗存。

vocabulary.entry: investigation /ɪnˌvestɪˈɡeɪʃn/ n. 调查，研究（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The police are conducting an investigation.
vocabulary.translation: 警方正在进行调查。

vocabulary.entry: tourist attraction /ˈtʊərɪst əˌtrækʃn/ n. 旅游景点（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The castle is a major tourist attraction.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城堡是一个主要的旅游景点。

vocabulary.definition: 外出走动，四处活动（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: out and about /ˌaʊt ənd əˈbaʊt/ phr. 外出走动，四处活动（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I've been out and about all day.
vocabulary.translation: 我一整天都在外面奔波。

vocabulary.entry: admire /ədˈmaɪə(r)/ v. 欣赏，钦佩
vocabulary.example: We stopped to admire the beautiful sunset.
vocabulary.translation: 我们停下来欣赏美丽的日落。

vocabulary.entry: beneath /bɪˈniːθ/ prep. 在……之下（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The ground beneath our feet was soft.
vocabulary.translation: 我们脚下的地面很软。
